"Let $P,Q$) be $d$-dimensional simplicial spheres, and let $FR(P)$ and $FR(Q)$ denote their facet-ridge graphs. **Kalai's reconstruction conjecture.** Every isomorphism between their facet-ridge graphs

$$
f: FR(P) \to FR(Q)
$$

has a unique extension to a simplicial isomorphism

$$
g: P \to Q.
$$

This extends the Blind–Mani theorem from simple polytopes to simplicial spheres; the conjecture is motivated by the fact that simplicial polytopes are reconstructible from their facet-ridge graphs, while general simplicial spheres may be non-polytopal."

"An **edge-colored complete graph** is a complete graph whose edges are assigned colors, and a PC Hamilton cycle is a spanning cycle whose consecutive edges have distinct colors.

**Gutin–Kim conjecture.** It is polynomial-time checkable whether an edge-colored complete graph contains a PC Hamilton cycle.

The paper notes that the conjecture is known for $2$-colored complete graphs via the characterization of Bánkfalvi and Bánkfalvi, while the general case is presented as open. A solution to the stated characterization problem for merging two vertex-disjoint PC cycles would be a major step toward this conjecture."

$$
\psi(D)=\sum_{v\in V(D)}\frac{1}{\deg^+(v)}.

**Seymour's non-uniform Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture.** $D$ contains a directed cycle of length at most

$$
\left\lceil\psi(D)\right\rceil.
$$
